newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says Karen rebels break off talks, some defect.
newsitem.headline: Burma says Karen rebels break off talks, some defect.

text.p: More than 500 members of the Karen National Union (KNU) rebel organisation have surrendered to Burma's military government after peace talks between the two sides were broken off, official television reported on Saturday.
State run television said the KNU, which had held four rounds of peace talks with the government, unilaterally broke off the negotitations.
"Some KNU leaders and members, who are in favour of peace, have defied control of the extremist central KNU leadership and have returned to the legal fold on their own volition," the broadcast said.

It said a total of 511 KNU members from two townships had surrendered since February 11. Burmese army officers said on Wednesday about 400 KNU guerrillas had surrendered to Burmese troops, although the KNU disputed the figure and said only 70 were involved.
It was not clear whether the 511 mentioned in the broadcast included the 400 mentioned earlier by Burmese officials.
The latest announcement comes amid reports from some top KNU sources of a possible split in the KNU which has been fighting for greater autonomy from Rangoon since it was founded in 1948.
The sources said hardline KNU leader General Bo Mya and moderate vice-president Swe Seing differed over how to deal with Rangoon's military government.

Swe Seing wants to soften the KNU stance and wants the peace talks to work while Bo Mya has repeatedly said the KNU would continue to fight against Burmese troops. His supporters say Bo Mya still commanded more than 15,000 guerrillas who were fighting Rangoon.

The KNU is one of the few rebel groups that has rejected Rangoon's peace overtures and refused to lay down arms. Fifteen other ethnic guerrilla groups have already reached ceasefire agreements with the military government.

Earlier this week a senior KNU spokesman, who fled with thousands of Karen refugees to the Thai side of the border with Burma after Burmese troops razed the group's key mobile jungle camps in Eastern Burma, called for peace talks with Rangoon.
The call for a truce came after the Thai military said it would squeeze out guerrillas from border camps.

The broadcast said Burma's army has had 53 "encounters" with KNU insurgents since February 11, resulting in the deaths of 41 KNU members. It said seven government soldiers were killed in the skirmishes and 32 others were injured.
